title: Olivia Colman Embraces Wicker's Viral Memes and IKEA Joke
excerpt:
The unusual romance Wicker has inspired an online wave of wicker-themed humor.
Olivia Colman and the cast have enjoyed the memes, baskets and IKEA's cheeky ad.
body_md:
A romance built around a woman who asks for a husband made of wicker was almost destined to become an internet talking point. Wicker has inspired a wave of playful reactions, and its cast has been following the jokes as enthusiastically as many viewers.

One standout came from IKEA's Australian social-media account, which promoted a wicker bench using a pun about being made from husband material. The advertisement spread among movie fans, and Olivia Colman has spoken warmly about the attention. The actors reportedly enjoyed seeing the concept of the film transformed into memes and everyday visual jokes.

The movie adapts Ursula Wills's short story The Wicker Husband, with Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson writing and directing. Alexander Skarsgård wore a physical wicker costume created by Wētā Workshop, giving the central fantasy an unusually tangible presence rather than relying entirely on digital effects.

Audiences have joined in by bringing wicker baskets to screenings, while a themed popcorn bucket has become another conversation piece. Some limited 4DX presentations added moving seats and effects such as falling snow, extending the film's eccentric atmosphere into the theater itself.

The response illustrates how a distinctive visual premise can generate a wider pop-cultural life through social media and audience participation. Viral jokes do not, however, establish how well the film has performed commercially.
seo_title: Olivia Colman Reacts to Wicker's Viral IKEA Memes
seo_description: Wicker has inspired an IKEA joke, basket-carrying moviegoers and viral memes that Olivia Colman and the cast have embraced.
